newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone coup soldiers, Nigerian troops clash.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone coup soldiers, Nigerian troops clash.

text.p: Soldiers staging a coup in Sierra Leone on Sunday exchanged sustained fire with Nigerian troops guarding the state house in the capital Freetown, witnesses said.

"An exchange of fire between Nigerian troops and coup-makers continues at state house," said one resident who lives near the city centre presidential office complex. There was no immediate word on casualties.
Nigerian and Guinean troops have been backing the Sierra Leone army in the country's rebel war. Nigerian troops guard the state house, the capital's international airport and other key sites.

Coup spokesman Corporal Gborie said in a radio broadcast that junior ranks in the army had toppled civilian President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who had fled the West African country. He asked Nigerian troops not to intervene in what he called an internal matter.

Small-arms fire and the occasional crash of mortar shells continued into the afternoon. A government building in the vicinity of the state house was on fire and other office blocks, including the treasury, were threatened, residents said.
